mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or notary in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certified copy and Hague Apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Judicial record authority (Casier judiciaire) in home state

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, managers, and signatories against the consolidated EU financial sanctions list, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, the US OFAC SDN list, and the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF) list. Enhanced due diligence and source-of-wealth documentation are required for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), their family members, and close associates.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – online portal at www.lbr.lu; maintained by Luxembourg Business Registers GIE.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be in French, German, Luxembourgish, English, or other Latin-script languages; if the desired name uses non-Latin characters, a Latin-script transliteration is mandatory. The legal form identifier 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or its abbreviation 'S.à r.l.' or 'SARL' must appear. Names must not be misleading and must comply with principles of distinctiveness.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the LBR rejects a proposed name, the applicant may, within 3 months from notification, bring an administrative appeal before the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) against the Grand-Duchy of Luxembourg, represented by the Minister of Justice. Prior to filing, the applicant may request a reasoned interpretation in writing from the LBR and may file a new name request. Extensions of a valid reservation are generally not granted after expiry; re-filing a new request with payment of the applicable fee restarts the 30-day window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Domiciliation services are permissible, but only with a licensed domiciliation agent; a mere virtual mailbox is insufficient to serve as the statutory registered office for a SARL. For the present low-risk Helpdesk SaaS industry, use of an approved domiciliation address is commercially accepted if board meeting locations and substance remain demonstrable in Luxembourg.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low – approximately 2% annual likelihood of an unannounced on-site inspection by the Luxembourg tax authorities or RCS attesting to substance. If the company relies solely on a virtual office, this probability rises to 10%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as consolidated (Title V, Chapter 2, Articles 710-1 to 710-27, Société à Responsabilité Limitée; Article 710-2 on capital; Article 710-3 on the constitutive deed; Article 711-1 on the registered office); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and the Publicity of Annual Accounts; Law of 2 September 2011 on the establishment permit, Article 7-2 (exemption of information-technology services); Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) of Luxembourg, operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) under the supervision of the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif (Articles of Association), signed before a Luxembourg notary or executed by private deed or electronic standardized instrument under the Law of 10 August 1915, accompanied by a declaration of conformity, filed on the RCS e-file platform and published in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital EUR 1 for a modernized SARL; capital must be fully subscribed and fully paid up in cash into a blocked escrow account opened in the future company's name with a Luxembourg credit institution; funds are released only upon RCS registration. If capital is below EUR 12,500, enhanced safeguards apply (in-kind contribution audit by a réviseur d'entreprises and a balance-sheet test before distributions and share buy-backs). Recommended standard capital: EUR 12,500.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS ADOPTED at the constitutive meeting of [Company Name], a Luxembourg Société à Responsabilité Limitée: 1. The draft Articles of Association are approved. The share capital of EUR 12,500.00, fully subscribed and paid into blocked account [IBAN] with [Bank], is ratified and declared available upon RCS registration. 2. The registered office is fixed at [Address], Luxembourg. 3. [Name] is appointed Sole Manager (Gérant) with full power to act alone and bind the Company lawfully, including all registration actions. 4. The Sole Manager is instructed to file the constitutive documents with the RCS, open operational bank accounts, and complete VAT and other regulatory formalities. So decided and signed at [Place], on [Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name availability screening and reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS — Luxembourg Business Registers; public consultation and company name search module at lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run an exact-match and fuzzy search of the proposed name against the RCS company database; verify the required corporate identifier (SARL or Société à Responsabilité Limitée); screen for conflicting trademarks on the IP Luxembourg register; prepare a written availability opinion with three ranked fallback names and secure the first available candidate for filing.
required_dossiers: Availability opinion memorandum with 3 candidate names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries identity with an earlier registered name, adopt the next fallback name and file a rectificative deed; a third-party trademark opposition is cured by written consent of the prior holder or substitution of the corporate suffix.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) for indirect taxes; central portal: MyGuichet.lu / guichet.lu; company register: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing an SARL must file the incorporation deed through a Luxembourg notary, obtain the RCS registration number, and be assigned the national identification number (matricule) which serves as the general TIN for direct tax purposes. A Luxembourg VAT number (N° TVA) must then be applied for with the AED through MyGuichet.lu. Non-resident entities without a Luxembourg establishment generally do not register for Luxembourg VAT if B2B supplies are reverse-charged to the customer or if B2C e-services are declared under the EU OSS; direct VAT registration is required only when the supply is treated as taxable in Luxembourg and no other simplification applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime; an SARL is automatically an opaque resident company subject to corporate income tax. Statutory elections include VAT grouping (assujetti unique) under Luxembourg VAT law, fiscal integration for corporate income tax for qualified groups, and waiver of the small-undertaking VAT exemption. Hybrid mismatch treatment is not elective; EU ATAD anti-hybrid rules apply.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for the small-undertaking VAT exemption; no general VAT registration threshold applies to established taxable persons. Non-resident suppliers of B2C e-services may use the EU OSS instead of local registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not impose real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, API-based reporting, or digital stamping. B2B e-invoicing is permitted when authenticity and integrity are ensured. E-invoicing is mandatory for invoices to Luxembourg central government entities using the PEPPOL-compatible EU standard.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods, 0% VAT applies where goods leave the EU under customs supervision and the supplier holds transport and export evidence; the export declaration and commercial documents must prove physical removal. For services, including helpdesk/SaaS supplies, B2B services to an overseas taxable person are outside Luxembourg VAT under place-of-supply rules and are generally reverse-charged; B2C e-services to non-EU consumers are outside Luxembourg VAT, while B2C e-services to EU consumers are taxable at destination and may be reported via OSS. Luxembourg law imposes no statutory FX repatriation deadline; 180 days is used only as a commercial documentation benchmark.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic via LU-CUS / EU AES)
Bill of Lading or equivalent transport evidence
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent payment evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AED may claw back VAT if export proof is not substantiated within the assessment window, with interest running from the original VAT due date. Fraudulent zero-rating or false documentation is treated as VAT fraud, leading to reassessment, administrative fines, criminal penalties, and extended limitation periods of up to 10 years in bad-faith cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) within the Eurosystem (ECB); financial-sector supervision is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). Luxembourg abolished exchange controls upon implementation of Directive 88/361/EEC and Article 63 TFEU; no ministry or central-bank prior authorization exists for cross-border payments or FX conversion.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro (EUR) is fully convertible for both current-account (subscription and helpdesk service revenue) and capital-account (equity injection, shareholder loans, dividend and profit remittance) transactions. No surrender, transfer, or notification requirements apply. Profit remittance hurdles are non-monetary: the SARL must satisfy the corporate-law balance-sheet and liquidity tests before distributions, and the domestic 15% dividend withholding tax (reduced to 0%-15% under tax treaties and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive) may apply. Foreign-currency (USD, GBP) accounts are freely permitted.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Luxembourg imposes no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation obligation on export proceeds from SaaS/helpdesk services. USD receipts collected through Stripe Billing and PayPal may be retained in a multi-currency account or converted at market rate at the discretion of the SARL's treasury policy.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow (compte séquestre/bloqué) + EUR Operational Current Account
Capital Escrow Account + Operational Multi-Currency Account (EUR/USD/GBP)
Operational Current Account + Multi-Currency Treasury Sub-Accounts
SME Operational Current Account with SEPA Cash Management
Operational Account + Global Transaction Banking / FX Line
Multi-Currency Operational Account + Treasury/FX Dealing Line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium. Luxembourg provides a modern PSD2 framework (CSSF-licensed payment and e-money institutions passported across the EEA), which suits payouts-only treasury functions. Legal constraints: EMIs are not credit institutions and cannot issue the capital-escrow attestation (attestation de blocage) required by Luxembourg notaries; they may not extend credit or hold idle commercial liquidity beyond payment-facilitation limits. Because the target rails are Stripe Billing (Stripe Payments Europe Ltd, Ireland) and PayPal (PayPal (Europe) S.à r.l. et Cie, S.C.A., a Luxembourg-licensed credit institution), the SARL should maintain a credit-institution account and use EMIs solely as an add-on acquiring and settlement layer.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Default: at least one natural-person manager/director and each UBO with a qualifying holding must attend an in-person onboarding interview or, for selected banks (BGL BNP Paribas, Intesa Sanpaolo), a CSSF-compliant remote video-KYC with eIDAS-qualified signatures. Fully remote opening is possible for a low-risk SaaS/helpdesk SARL only when corporate documents are apostilled and legalized, UBO source-of-funds is documented, and a Luxembourg regulated fiduciary (notary, CSFF/PSF, or authorized accountant) signs the client-introduction certificate. BCEE and BIL generally require a physical presence step.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity low-ticket receivables: large monthly flows of Stripe/PayPal subscription payments, refunds and chargebacks concentrated on a small-balance sheet.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant-of-record agreements with Stripe and PayPal; chargeback/refund SOP and dispute log; PCI-DSS Level 1 attestation; 12-month MRR/ARPU/churn report; customer concentration by jurisdiction; GDPR-compliant data-processing agreements; statutory audit pack of the SaaS helpdesk platform.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or offshore shareholding with nominee local manager, raising UBO and source-of-wealth opacity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RBE (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) filing extract; notarized statutory articles with full ownership chain; UBO passports and bank-referenced source-of-funds statements; no-trust/no-nominee declaration; Luxembourg tax-residence certificate (attestation de résidence fiscale) request if disputed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and AML exposure of global helpdesk end-users and risk of circumventing EU restrictive measures via cloud software.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EU/OFAC/UK sanctions screening policy with automated geoblocking; no EAR/dual-use controlled code statement; subscription terms prohibiting sanctioned persons; annual SOC 2 Type II report; suspicious-transaction reporting process to the Luxembourg FIU (Cellule de Renseignements Financiers) in place.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Letter-box substance concern: customer-support and helpdesk functions outsourced abroad with minimal Luxembourg payroll and premises.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg lease or co-working occupancy agreement; local employment contracts with Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) registrations; payroll journal; 24-month cash-flow plan; annual accounts prepared by a licensed Luxembourg accountant and filed with the RCS.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Share subscriptions are wired by SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank to a blocked escrow (compte séquestre) at the Luxembourg bank using purpose code DE/EQTY (direct-investment equity) with reference 'capital subscription LU_SARL'; the bank issues the attestation de blocage to the notary before incorporation. Post-incorporation capital increases require a notarized shareholders' resolution and transfer via TARGET2/SEPA on a dedicated equity IBAN; USD injections are converted at the ECB reference rate plus margin or ring-fenced as a USD sub-account equity tranche. Verification: proof of source of funds (dividend minutes, disposal agreements), CSSF-preserved account statements, and publication of the capital increase with the RCS.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EU/SEPA rails: SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant for payroll, CCSS social-security contributions, and EU cloud/SaaS vendors (Microsoft, AWS-EU) via EBICS/API. Non-EU rails: SWIFT MT103 for USD/GBP service invoices and subcontractor settlements (India, Philippines), transmitted with ISO 20022 pain.001 and structured remittance fields (INV./PO./tax-ref); daily Stripe/PayPal payouts are swept to the EUR operational account while USD payouts remain in a USD sub-account pending FX decision. Commercial letters of credit are not required for a pure helpdesk-SaaS model; standby LC/guarantee facilities at BGL/BIL apply only to enterprise government tenders.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD FX forward (up to 12 months; IFEMA/ISDA short-form with the operating bank) for committed USD receivables.
EUR/USD FX swap (spot-next/tom-next) for efficient rolling of daily Stripe/PayPal USD balances.

Plain-vanilla EUR/USD zero-cost collar or currency option where any IC-enterprise revenue concentration exceeds USD 250,000 per quarter; speculative option strategies are prohibited by SARL treasury policy.
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) only for residual exotic-cross subcontractor currencies (PHP, INR) if bank lines permit; EUR/USD NDFs are economically unnecessary given full euro convertibility.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual financial statements (annual accounts)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés / RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the financial year-end (e.g., 31 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers monetary fines (typically up to EUR 10,000) and, after repeated or continued default, judicial strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax / net wealth tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by 31 May of the following tax year or by 30 June when filed by a certified tax advisor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers default interest (0.6% per month), an administrative fine up to EUR 5,000, and possible forced taxation assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (RBE return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Beneficial Owners Register (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs / RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within one month of the latest RBE confirmation anniversary; any UBO change must be filed within 1 month of the triggering event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance or false declarations are punishable by fines up to EUR 125,000 and possible imprisonment of directors or officers.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is required where a SARL exceeds two of three thresholds: total balance sheet above EUR 4.4 million; net turnover above EUR 8.8 million; average number of employees above 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002, as amended; aligns with EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS permitted for consolidated financial statements only.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must annually reconfirm the accuracy of beneficial owner data filed with the RBE. Any transfer of membership interests resulting in a UBO change must be declared within 1 month; failure to update or to confirm triggers criminal penalties under the UBO Law.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (register of parts sociales / shares

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - 2,500 per year for registered office and local corporate secretarial agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - 15,000 per year for a typical small-to-mid-size SARL statutory audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No blanket tax holiday is available. Relevant incentives for a customer-support/helpdesk SaaS company include the Luxembourg IP tax regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income where software is patented), the R&D tax credit (20%-25% of eligible research and development expenses), accelerated depreciation on intangible assets and servers, and the possibility of an advance tax ruling confirming the effective rate. Such incentives reduce the effective cash tax rate below the 24.94% combined statutory headline rate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory time limit; losses carry forward indefinitely under Luxembourg tax code, subject to continuity-of-enterprise and anti-churning rules)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 3 (Déclaration pour l’impôt sur les sociétés) – filed electronically through MyGuichet / eDéclaration and the Luxembourg Interconnection Framework (LIF) portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 May of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end for calendar-year filers; automatic statutory extension to 31 December where the return is prepared by a registered Luxembourg tax adviser (common practice)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RCS registration number, Luxembourg tax matriculation number, VAT number, registered office address, and the tax year period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact legal name and RCS number of the Luxembourg SARL; state the non-resident UBOs in the accompanying UBO declaration and notify any change of directors.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Description of the effective business carried on: multi-channel omnichannel helpdesk and conversational bot cloud, SaaS customer support platform, no statutory license required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe the employee structure, physical office in Luxembourg, and the role of non-resident group entities in delivering or supporting the service. Specify payment rails (Stripe, PayPal) in the notes to the tax return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciling LUX GAAP accounting profit to taxable corporate income: add non-deductible expenses, subtract exempt intellectual property income (if patent box applies), R&D tax credits, participation exemption, and prior-year loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a Luxembourg fiscal statement (Etat des résultats) and a loss carryforward schedule in EUR; foreign-currency subscription revenue from non-resident customers must be converted at the ECB closing rate, and all intercompany billing must be supported by transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 17 – Withholding tax and tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of the amount of corporate income tax prepaid (payments d’acompte), dividends distributed during the fiscal year, and any withholding tax credits to be offset.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For any distribution to a non-resident shareholder claiming treaty or Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief, attach the completed Luxembourg withholding-tax exemption form (Form 1) and the shareholder’s Tax Residence Certificate; otherwise declare the 15% dividend WHT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of controlled transactions: helpdesk fees, software licensing or cost reimbursement with group entities; a functional analysis, transfer-pricing method selected, and arm’s-length range must be disclosed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident parent or affiliate must supply a Master File/Local File and a benchmark study demonstrating that the Luxembourg entity receives an arm’s-length profit for its customer-support functions, including employee costs and a market-based markup.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty from EUR 5,000 for a first offence to EUR 25,000 for repeated non-filing, plus a 10% statutory increase on the assessed tax (majoration) if the return is not filed within the prescribed grace period. Late payment interest accrues at 0.8% per month on the unpaid corporate income tax; continued non-payment triggers enforced collection against the SARL and personal liability of managers in cases of intent or serious negligence.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a double taxation agreement (DTA) or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (PSD), the non-resident shareholder must file a written request for exemption or reduced withholding tax with the Luxembourg direct tax administration (ACD) before the dividend is payable. The application must include a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder’s residence state, a statement that the shareholder is the beneficial owner, proof of the minimum qualifying holding (e.g., 10% or EUR 1.2 million acquisition cost under PSD), and a commitment to inform the Luxembourg tax authority of any subsequent misuse. An advance ruling or formal confirmation can be obtained via the ACD's 'Bulletin de Renseignements' procedure. Failure to comply results in the full 15% WHT being applied and a re-opening of prior assessments under the Luxembourg GAAR.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg does not impose domestic withholding tax on outbound royalties or debt interest, whether paid to EU or non-EU residents; the statutory rate is therefore 0%. Under Luxembourg’s tax treaties and the EU Interest & Royalties Directive, the residual treaty rate for qualifying related companies is also 0%, provided the recipient is the beneficial owner and the arrangements are not artificial. Arm’s-length pricing and economic-substance conditions remain enforceable.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Master File and Local File are required where the Luxembourg SARL belongs to a multinational group with consolidated annual turnover of at least EUR 50 million and the SARL itself has net turnover above EUR 5 million or enters into cross-border controlled transactions exceeding EUR 100,000 per annum. In all other cases, a contemporaneous arm’s-length benchmarking study should nevertheless be prepared and made available to the ACD within 30 days of request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) of the Gulf Cooperation Council type. However, the ACD enforces substance-over-form through the national anti-abuse rule (Article 6 ATA), the EU ATAD interest limitation and CFC rules, and the OECD BEPS minimum standards. The benefit of tax treaties, the Parent-Subsidiary Directive, the Interest & Royalties Directive, and the participation exemption are denied where the Luxembourg SARL is a pure letterbox company without employees, premises, business activities, and effective management in Luxembourg.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly underreporting subscription revenues collected through Stripe and PayPal, issuing fabricated invoices for non-existent helpdesk services, or deleting transactional records with intent to reduce taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under Luxembourg tax law (Article 396 LIR): imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years and a fine of up to EUR 125,000, increased to five times that amount for a corporate entity; in addition, the tax administration reopens the fiscal year, imposes a 100% late-filing addition in aggravated cases, and levies monthly late-payment interest of 0.8% on the reassessed tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and statutory managers are personally and jointly liable for the corporate income tax, withholding tax, and VAT debts if the evasion is attributable to their intentional fault. Courts can order travel bans, seizure of personal bank accounts, disqualification from board service, and imprisonment in connection with the underlying tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging the Luxembourg helpdesk entity an intentionally low or zero margin while shifting profits to a related software vendor; failing to prepare or submit the Local File and Master File upon audit; using an unsupported CUP when the SaaS model requires a functional analysis under TNMM; creating retroactive invoices without time-sheet or service delivery evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Luxembourg tax authorities re-determine the taxable income under the arm’s-length principle, impose a corporate income tax increase and municipal business tax recalculated at 24.94%, add a penalty equal to the full tax reassessed when the failure is persistent, and apply 0.8% monthly interest. In egregious intra-group financing cases, thin-capitalisation and ATAD interest limitation rules deny a deduction and reclassify distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or sign an intercompany service agreement without a functional and economic analysis, or who ignore a documented tax-advice warning, may be held personally liable for the resulting tax shortfall and penalties; under Luxembourg insolvency law, they may also face court-imposed personal contribution orders and a professional ban for mismanagement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / absence of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Luxembourg SARL solely as a conduit to channel customer-support revenue, license fees, or dividends without maintaining real employees, an office, decision-making authority, or operational expenditure commensurate with the recorded service activity; board meetings not held in Luxembourg; no participation of the Luxembourg entity in group commercial functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of tax treaty benefits, denial of the Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption, and recapture of 15% withholding tax on gross distributions; the tax administration re-assesses the entire profit under the substance-over-form doctrine, adds a 10% tax increase, and in cross-border situations may report the arrangement as a sham using the EU joint transfer-pricing forum and OECD anti-BEPS toolkits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors and effective managers incur personal liability under Luxembourg company law (law of 10 August 1915) for losses caused by maintaining a letterbox structure; civil restitution orders, personal fines up to EUR 125,000, and mandatory travel bans are available; in insolvency proceedings, the manager’s personal assets may be used to satisfy corporate tax liabilities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / KYC and UBO disclosure failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting the non-resident ultimate beneficial owner from the Luxembourg trade register and the AML UBO register, failing to perform risk-based due diligence on Stripe/PayPal transactions exceeding statutory thresholds, or not reporting anomalous cash flows to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU); refusal to produce an updated shareholders register in a tax audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CSSF administrative fines up to EUR 1 million or 10% of the annual turnover of the SARL; the tax administration can invalidate the tax return and re-open the statute of limitations under fraud time limits (10 years); proceedings under the Luxembourg anti-money laundering law can trigger fines equivalent to the amount laundered and imprisonment of up to five years for responsible natural persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal punishment for AML breaches, including imprisonment of eight days to five years and criminal fines; they may also be prohibited indefinitely from serving as board members of any Luxembourg company, while seizure of personal assets and EU-wide travel bans can be issued in the context of a money-laundering investigation.
